solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: President given degree by primate

parts.note: George Bush, US President, father or son
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US president receives an honorary degree from an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is just a link joining the president to the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby, or galago, is a small nocturnal African primate with huge eyes.

clue.text: Divide portion with dry inside

indicators.note: the dry word goes inside the portion word

parts.note: a bit is a small portion
sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Split a share with something dry in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, to divide.

clue.text: Eats out sadly with what reportedly leads to suspension of free representation

indicators.note: the letters of eats and out are put in a sorry, rearranged state
the sound is heard rather than spelt, giving letters that sound alike

parts.note: flibberty-gibbet: the first part leads on to gibbet, a gallows for hanging

explanation.surface: A gloomy diner and a prelude to hanging somehow suggest a free image.
explanation.walkthrough: EATS OUT rearranged gives STATUEO; 'flibberty' is the first half of flibbertigibbet, and leads to gibbet, the gallows. 'what' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York statue is a sculpted representation of Liberty, the personification of freedom.

clue.text: Bombs successful at the box office?

definitions.meaning: large Second World War bombs able to destroy a whole city ...
hit films that draw big crowds

explanation.definitionFit: Large aerial bombs of the 1940s, and also hugely popular films.

clue.text: See 3
Silly little boy keeping sheep

indicators.note: the boy's name holds the sheep inside it, as a keeper holds something

parts.note: Sid is a short form of the boy's name Sidney
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A foolish small lad looks after a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a silly person is a foolish, witless one.

clue.text: Musician's winning card starts for ever

parts.note: a trump card beats cards of other suits

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the word for for ever are kept

parts.note: eternity means for ever

explanation.surface: An instrumentalist always holds the winning card.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a musician who plays the trumpet.

clue.text: Fit representation turned out half the price

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A painting went for half price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like one phrase, but 'turned' alone signals the anagram of OUT HALF THE PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as this phrase looks perfectly well, an image of fitness.

clue.text: First of doctors to study flu, possibly? That's very bad

indicators.note: the opening letter of doctors is taken

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: the letters of flu could possibly be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A doctor researching influenza finds it nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadful means terrible or extremely bad.

clue.text: Start on cocaine said, with heroin, to affect the hippocampus?

indicators.note: the letter picked is spoken, and its name sounds like a body of water
the opening letter of the word cocaine is taken

parts.note: horse is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Drugs taken together might damage the brain's memory centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The hippocampus is a part of the brain, but its name is Greek for this creature; 'affect' here means take on the look of, as in affecting a style.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippocampus is the zoological genus name of the small upright fish with a horse-like head.

clue.text: Man following king abandoning fast food

indicators.note: the man's word comes after the shortened word
the king's letter leaves the word for fast, so it is removed

parts.note: quick means fast
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man trails a monarch who is giving up his fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' reads as a phrase, but 'fast' belongs to the wordplay and 'food' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury egg-custard tart, an example of a dish of food.

clue.text: Make representation of raffle

definitions.meaning: to sketch or depict a picture of something
a lottery in which tickets are pulled out at random

explanation.definitionFit: To sketch a picture, and a lottery where prizes are picked by chance.

clue.text: Solid piece or larger one numbered

parts.note: given a number, here C, the Roman numeral for a hundred
a hunk is a large piece, bigger than the solid piece defined

explanation.surface: A lump of something, or a bigger lump with a number on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'numbered' supplies the Roman numeral C attached to the front of the larger piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A chunk is a thick solid lump of something, like a chunk of cheese.

clue.text: Poet of rap breaking into English with singular old oath

indicators.note: the word rap forces its way inside the oath
the oath is made singular, so its plural ending is dropped

parts.note: zounds, from God's wounds, is an archaic exclamation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet of hip-hop bursts onto the English scene with an old-fashioned curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking into English' suggests the rapper breaks into the English scene; in fact the rap breaks into the oath, and 'singular' trims the plural from 'God's wounds'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American modernist poet, author of The Cantos.

clue.text: Cult's periodic distortion of fundamentals of crime

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are bent out of shape and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of cult plus the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A religious sect regularly twists its doctrines.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses every letter of CULTS PERIODIC, including the possessive S.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for body of the offence, the legal term for the facts that prove a crime was committed.

clue.text: Dickensian hypocrite's use of beak and nose

parts.note: a bird pecks with its beak
to sniff is to use the nose

explanation.surface: A two-faced character relies on his mouth and nose.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth Pecksniff is the sanctimonious hypocrite in Dickens's Martin Chuzzlewit; 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth Pecksniff in Martin Chuzzlewit is a byword for unctuous hypocrisy.

clue.text: Painter in view at tea, unexpectedly

indicators.note: the painter's name lies inside the following run of words

explanation.surface: An artist appears suddenly while people are at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' looks like an anagram signal, but the name runs straight through vieW AT TEA Unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Antoine Watteau was an eighteenth-century French painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: Lent to be progressive

definitions.meaning: loaned, as money is ... to a borrower

explanation.definitionFit: Money paid ahead of time, and modern or forward-looking ideas.

clue.text: See 14
Fourth article — one was terrible

parts.note: IV is the Roman numeral four
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fourth item recalls a dreadful ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar Ivan IV of Russia was known as Ivan the Terrible.

clue.text: Container used by painter in teashop

indicators.note: the painter's letters go inside the teashop

parts.note: a café is a place serving tea and snacks
RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist in a café pours from a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass vessel for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: Reptile from Virginia?

definitions.meaning: a crawling creature, a creeping thing

explanation.definitionFit: Something that creeps along the ground, and a climbing plant named after Virginia.

clue.text: Common standard and not royal town

parts.note: bog-standard is slang for common or ordinary
nor means and not

explanation.surface: An ordinary, not royal, seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: BOGNOR Regis is an English seaside town on the Sussex coast, given 'Regis' after George V convalesced there.
explanation.definitionFit: Bognor Regis takes its royal suffix from George V's stay there in 1929.

clue.text: Surprise attack by rebel on morning transport

indicators.note: in a down light the rebel sits on top; here it simply follows the morning transport

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, means morning
a bus is a form of transport
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: Insurgents ambush the early bus.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an old word for an ambush, troops lying in wait to attack.

clue.text: Belief of revolutionary in company

indicators.note: the revolutionary goes inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A firm takes on a radical's convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, Latin for I believe, is a statement of faith or creed.

clue.text: Churchman sounds as if he should be fired

indicators.note: the clergyman's title is heard like a weapon's name

parts.note: a cannon is a gun fired in battle

explanation.surface: A clergyman's title suggests he ought to be sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' seems to mean dismissed from a job; it is a gun being fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a clergyman attached to a cathedral chapter.

clue.text: Raven heard in former steel town

indicators.note: the town's name is spoken, giving a Scottish word of the same sound

parts.note: Corby in Northamptonshire was a steel-making town until the 1980s

explanation.surface: A big black bird is heard in an old industrial town.
explanation.walkthrough: CORBY, an English town in Northamptonshire whose steelworks closed in 1980, sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbie is a Scots word for a raven or crow, from French corbeau.

clue.text: Write to new pal on outside, there being no inside walls?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside the word for write
the letters of pal and on are made new, reshuffled

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone writes to a new friend about a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram of the two short words, and 'outside' puts the result around the writing word, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-plan office or home has few or no internal partitions dividing the floor space.

clue.text: Welcome break, bad time when inverted?

indicators.note: the phrase for a bad time is turned round word by word

parts.note: a day is a period of time
off means bad, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A holiday is good, but turned round it means a poor performance.
explanation.walkthrough: An OFF DAY is a bad time; swap the two words and you get a welcome break.
explanation.definitionFit: A day free from work or duties is a welcome break from routine.

clue.text: Board for one at digs?

definitions.meaning: an old wooden platter for serving food
someone who digs trenches, with 'digs' also suggesting lodgings

explanation.definitionFit: An old wooden plate, and also a person who cuts trenches.
